verticals.name: HVAC
verticals.industry_context:
HVAC work mixes emergency repairs, planned maintenance and system replacements. Repairs arrive as inbound calls that someone has to answer and dispatch, maintenance runs on recurring visits, and replacements are large jobs that need a clear quote and a way to pay over time. HVAC software is judged on how well it handles all three.

Residential and commercial HVAC are served by different tools. Housecall Pro and Jobber are built for home service businesses, and ServiceTitan serves both residential and commercial trades businesses with larger teams. BuildOps is built for commercial mechanical, electrical, plumbing and HVAC contractors that run both service and project work, and it is not built for residential work.

Maintenance agreements are one place the platforms differ. ServiceTitan lists membership management as a key feature, FieldEdge includes service agreements with renewal and billing automation, and Housecall Pro adds recurring service plans on its MAX plan. Jobber supports recurring jobs and visits but does not sell a dedicated membership-plan module.
verticals.buying_personas:
What an HVAC business needs from software depends mostly on its size and its mix of work.

If you work alone or with a small crew, start with tools you can test on real jobs before you pay. Jobber and Housecall Pro both publish their prices and offer 14-day free trials. The How to choose section on this page lists the tools whose stated team size fits a small shop.

If you run several techs and an office, check how each plan charges as you add people. Service Fusion charges a flat company price with unlimited users at every tier, while Housecall Pro's plans include a set number of users (1, 5 or 8) and charge for more. If you sell maintenance agreements or buy ads, test agreement billing and call tracking before you sign (Housecall Pro has a 14-day free trial; Service Fusion lists no free trial).

If you run a large or multi-location operation, ServiceTitan is built for established businesses with larger teams that want depth in dispatch, marketing attribution and reporting. It publishes no prices and says its pricing is per technician, so get a written quote for your team size. FieldEdge is also quote-only, and its plans include 2, 4 or 6 mobile app licenses.

If most of your work is commercial service and project work, compare BuildOps, which covers service agreements, project management and AIA pay applications.
verticals.feature_priorities:
Features to test for HVAC work:

Maintenance agreements: automatic renewal billing, scheduled visits, renewal reminders and a flag that tells the dispatcher a caller is a plan member. ServiceTitan lists membership management, FieldEdge service agreements, and Housecall Pro recurring service plans on MAX; Jobber handles recurring jobs and visits without a membership-plan module.

Financing inside the quote: a replacement is a large purchase, and a monthly payment option shown in the quote lets the customer apply without leaving it. Housecall Pro and Jobber offer Wisetack financing on quotes, ServiceTitan works with GreenSky, Financeit and Service Finance, FieldEdge with GreenSky and the Optimus marketplace, and Workiz with Sunbit. Ask who pays the lender's fee.

Flat-rate pricebook: every tech charges the same price for the same job. FieldEdge and Housecall Pro (from Essentials) offer flat-rate pricing, and ServiceTitan's pricebook can pull supplier price changes through Pricebook Connect.

Call and ad tracking: if you buy ads, check whether the tool ties each call and booked job back to the ad. ServiceTitan's Marketing Pro ties calls, booked jobs and revenue back to the campaign, ad group or keyword, and FieldEdge tracks the lead source of incoming calls.

Dispatch and call answering on busy days: ServiceTitan's Dispatch Pro assigns jobs using technician skills, location, recent sales performance and conversion rates, and Workiz's Genius Answering (by plan or add-on) answers missed calls and books jobs.
verticals.regulatory_notes:
Rules that affect what HVAC software should record:

EPA Section 608: technicians who maintain, service, repair or dispose of equipment that could release refrigerants must be certified, so keep each tech's certification on file.

Refrigerant records: EPA rules require refrigerant records for some equipment and activities, so check whether a platform can log refrigerant added and recovered on each job or whether you need a separate tracker.

Newer refrigerants: R-454B and R-32 are classed as mildly flammable (A2L) and come with their own handling and installation requirements, so equipment records that show which refrigerant a system uses help techs prepare.

Licensing: states and cities license HVAC contractors differently, so a shop working in more than one jurisdiction needs to track each license and its renewal date.

Local rules and permits: some jurisdictions set noise limits or setbacks for outdoor units, and replacements can need permits. Ask any vendor whether it tracks permits or connects to your city's permit portal.
verticals.seasonality:
HVAC demand follows the weather: cooling calls rise in hot spells and heating calls in cold snaps, and when each arrives depends on your climate.

Peak weeks are when dispatch and call answering are tested, so check how a tool handles a full board and missed calls before the season starts. The quieter weeks between seasons are the time to sell maintenance agreements, book tune-ups, follow up on replacement quotes, and set up or switch software.

vertical_faqs.q: Which HVAC software fits a 3-tech shop?
vertical_faqs.a: Start with tools that publish prices and offer a trial, and run the same week of real jobs through each. Jobber (Connect plan from $99 a month billed annually) and Housecall Pro (Essentials, $149 a month billed annually with 5 users included) both publish their plans, offer 14-day free trials and add Wisetack financing to quotes. Service Fusion charges a flat company price with unlimited users at every tier (from $208 a month billed annually), which matters more as headcount grows. Jobber's QuickBooks sync covers QuickBooks Online only, so check that against your accountant's setup.

vertical_faqs.q: How do membership plans work in HVAC software?
vertical_faqs.a: A membership, or maintenance agreement, is a recurring plan: the customer pays a set fee for scheduled maintenance visits plus whatever extras you include, such as priority service or a repair discount. In software, look for automatic renewal billing, visit scheduling, renewal reminders and a member flag for dispatchers. ServiceTitan lists membership management as a key feature; FieldEdge includes service agreements with renewal and billing automation; Housecall Pro adds recurring service plans on its MAX plan; Jobber supports recurring jobs and visits but does not sell a dedicated membership-plan module, so test renewals and plan billing during the trial.

vertical_faqs.q: Does HVAC software need to handle commercial work?
vertical_faqs.a: Only if you do commercial work. Commercial project work (subcontractors, progress billing, AIA pay applications) needs features that residential service tools may not have. BuildOps is built for commercial mechanical, electrical, plumbing and HVAC contractors that run both service and project work, and it is not built for residential work. Housecall Pro and Jobber are built for home service businesses, and ServiceTitan serves both residential and commercial trades businesses. Pick by your own work mix.

vertical_faqs.q: How important is Google Local Services Ads integration for HVAC?
vertical_faqs.a: It matters if you get calls from Local Services Ads. Jobber, Housecall Pro and Workiz list Google Local Services Ads integrations, and ServiceTitan's Marketing Pro ties calls, booked jobs and revenue back to the campaign, ad group or keyword. Whatever you use, set up tracking so you can see which ads produce booked jobs.

vertical_faqs.q: What about AI features in HVAC software?
vertical_faqs.a: Ask what each AI feature does and test it on your own calls before you pay for it. Examples from our data: ServiceTitan's Dispatch Pro assigns jobs using technician skills, location, recent sales performance and conversion rates; Workiz's Genius Answering (by plan or add-on) answers missed calls and books jobs; Jobber's Plus plan includes an AI Receptionist that answers calls and texts.

verticals.name: Plumbing
verticals.industry_context:
Plumbing work runs from emergency calls (burst pipes, backups, no hot water) through scheduled service to large jobs such as water heater replacements, repipes and sewer line work. Emergency calls need someone to answer and a tech who can be dispatched quickly, large jobs need clear quotes and a way to offer financing, and scheduled work needs reminders and recurring visits.

Tools on this page lean toward different parts of that mix. Workiz is built around inbound, same-day calls, and its Genius Answering (by plan or add-on) answers missed calls and books jobs. For large jobs, Housecall Pro and Jobber add Wisetack financing to quotes, and ServiceTitan offers GreenSky, Financeit and Service Finance.

Some plumbing shops sell maintenance plans, such as a yearly drain cleaning or water heater flush with priority service. ServiceTitan (membership management), FieldEdge (service agreements) and Housecall Pro (recurring service plans on MAX) handle plan billing in the software; Jobber handles recurring jobs and visits without a membership-plan module.
verticals.buying_personas:
What a plumbing business needs from software depends on its size and its mix of emergency, scheduled and project work.

If you work alone or with a small crew, compare tools you can try before you pay. Jobber and Housecall Pro publish prices and offer 14-day free trials. Workiz quotes its prices on request, offers a 7-day free trial and is built around inbound, same-day calls, which suits shops whose work is mostly emergencies.

If you run several techs with an office, check how plans charge as you add people (Service Fusion charges a flat company price with unlimited users; Housecall Pro's plans include a set number of users) and whether the QuickBooks edition you use is supported: Service Fusion, Housecall Pro and FieldEdge list both QuickBooks Online and Desktop, and Jobber lists Online only.

If you run a large residential operation, ServiceTitan is built for established businesses with larger teams that want depth in dispatch, marketing attribution and reporting, and FieldEdge for HVAC, plumbing and electrical contractors who run QuickBooks; neither publishes prices. Commercial plumbing contractors that run service and project work can compare BuildOps.
verticals.feature_priorities:
Features to test for plumbing work:

After-hours calls: if you take emergency work, check how the tool routes calls outside office hours and what happens to a missed call. Workiz includes a phone system and call masking, and its Genius Answering (by plan or add-on) answers missed calls and books jobs; Service Fusion lists a VoIP phone system, with integrated voice from its Plus plan.

Financing for large jobs: Housecall Pro and Jobber add Wisetack financing to quotes, ServiceTitan works with GreenSky, Financeit and Service Finance, FieldEdge with GreenSky and the Optimus marketplace, and Workiz with Sunbit.

Flat-rate pricing: a pricebook keeps prices consistent across techs for common jobs such as drain cleaning or a water heater install. FieldEdge and Housecall Pro (from Essentials) offer flat-rate pricing, and ServiceTitan's pricebook can pull supplier price changes through Pricebook Connect.

Call and ad tracking: ServiceTitan's Marketing Pro ties calls, booked jobs and revenue back to the campaign, ad group or keyword; Jobber, Housecall Pro and Workiz integrate with Google Local Services Ads.

Video calls: if you want to diagnose simple problems by video before sending a truck, ask each vendor whether video calls are built in or need a separate tool.
verticals.regulatory_notes:
Rules that affect what plumbing software should record:

Licensing: states and cities license plumbers and plumbing contractors differently, so track each license, its holder and its renewal date, especially if you work in more than one jurisdiction.

Backflow testing: where your water authority requires certified backflow testers, track each tech's certification and its expiry date, and keep test reports with the job.

Lead-free materials: federal law requires pipes, fittings and fixtures used for drinking water to be lead free, so check that the products in your pricebook meet that standard.

Permits: water heater swaps, gas line work and sewer replacements can need permits, depending on your jurisdiction. Ask any vendor whether it tracks permits or connects to your city's portal.

Trenching: sewer line excavation falls under OSHA's excavation standards, so keep safety training records for the crews who dig.
verticals.seasonality:
Freezing weather bursts pipes, so a cold snap can bring a run of emergency calls. Check how a tool handles a full board and after-hours calls before winter.

Quieter periods are the time to sell maintenance plans, follow up on replacement quotes and set up or switch software; your own job history shows which months those are.

vertical_faqs.q: Which plumbing software fits a 3-tech shop?
vertical_faqs.a: Jobber (Connect plan from $99 a month billed annually) and Housecall Pro (Essentials, $149 a month billed annually with 5 users included) both publish prices, offer 14-day free trials and add Wisetack financing to quotes, so you can run the same week of jobs through both. If most of your work is emergency calls, also look at Workiz, which is built around inbound, same-day calls (prices on request, 7-day free trial).

vertical_faqs.q: How do plumbing membership plans work?
vertical_faqs.a: A plan is a recurring agreement, such as a yearly fee for drain cleaning or a water heater flush plus priority service; you decide what it includes. ServiceTitan (membership management), FieldEdge (service agreements with renewal and billing automation) and Housecall Pro (recurring service plans on MAX) handle plan billing in the software. Jobber supports recurring jobs and visits but does not sell a dedicated membership-plan module, so test renewals and plan billing during the trial.

vertical_faqs.q: Does plumbing software need to handle commercial work?
vertical_faqs.a: It depends on the work. For commercial service calls, check that the tool handles commercial customers (several sites per customer, purchase orders, payment terms). For commercial project work such as new construction or large multifamily jobs, you need project features such as progress billing: BuildOps is built for commercial mechanical, electrical, plumbing and HVAC contractors running both service and project work, with progress billing and AIA pay applications. Pick based on your work mix.

vertical_faqs.q: How important is after-hours / emergency call handling?
vertical_faqs.a: It matters if you sell emergency service: a caller with a burst pipe who reaches voicemail can call the next plumber on the list. Check how each tool routes after-hours calls to the on-call tech and what happens to a missed call. Workiz's Genius Answering (by plan or add-on) answers missed calls and books jobs.

vertical_faqs.q: Should plumbing shops use video-call diagnostics?
vertical_faqs.a: Some problems, such as a running toilet or a water heater error code, can be looked at on a video call before you send a truck. If you want to try it, run it on a small share of inbound calls and track how many turn into booked visits. Ask each vendor whether video calls are built in or need a separate tool.

verticals.name: Electrical
verticals.industry_context:
Electrical contractors split between service work (troubleshooting, panel upgrades, EV charger installs, code corrections) and project work (new construction, commercial buildouts, multifamily). The two need different software: service work runs on scheduling, dispatch and invoicing, while project work runs on job costing, change orders and progress billing.

Electrical work has to meet code, and work beyond minor repairs can need a permit and an inspection. The National Electrical Code is revised on a regular cycle, and states and cities adopt editions on their own schedules and may add their own amendments. Check what a platform offers for permit tracking before you buy, and expect to keep a separate tracker if it offers none.

For service work, Jobber and Housecall Pro are built for home service businesses, FieldEdge for HVAC, plumbing and electrical contractors who run QuickBooks, and ServiceTitan for established residential and commercial businesses with larger teams. For project work, Knowify offers job costing, change orders and AIA progress billing on QuickBooks, and BuildOps covers service and project work for commercial contractors. Contractors who do both either run two platforms or pick one built for both.

Solar and battery work is quoted in solar design tools. Aurora Solar, listed on our solar page, sizes batteries and in September 2026 added quoting for EV chargers and batteries for US installers.
verticals.buying_personas:
Which tools fit depends on whether your work is mostly service, mostly projects, or both.

Service-focused shops: Jobber and Housecall Pro publish their prices and offer 14-day free trials, and both add Wisetack financing to quotes for jobs such as panel upgrades and EV charger installs. FieldEdge (quote-only) is built for HVAC, plumbing and electrical contractors on QuickBooks, and ServiceTitan (quote-only) for established businesses with larger teams.

Shops with service and project work: Knowify adds job costing, change orders and AIA progress billing on QuickBooks (subcontracts and job costing start on its Advanced plan), and BuildOps covers both service and project work for commercial contractors.

Commercial project contractors: BuildOps is built for commercial mechanical, electrical, plumbing and HVAC contractors, and Procore for commercial general contractors, specialty contractors and owners on complex multi-trade projects; Procore is priced by annual construction volume with unlimited users.
verticals.feature_priorities:
Features to test for electrical work:

Permit tracking: applications, status and inspection dates in the job record rather than in a spreadsheet. Ask each vendor to show it, and whether it connects to your municipality's permit portal.

Code references: if your techs look up code requirements in the field, ask whether a platform offers code references or whether they will keep using a separate app.

Multi-part quotes: a panel upgrade, a new circuit and an EV charger install can go on one quote with line items in service tools such as Jobber, Housecall Pro and ServiceTitan. Solar with battery storage is quoted in solar design tools such as Aurora Solar.

Photos: photos taken before walls are closed (boxes, panel terminations, grounding) are a record of the work if an inspector or customer asks later. CompanyCam, a photo documentation app, lists integrations with ServiceTitan and Jobber, and Housecall Pro lists CompanyCam among its integrations.

Service and project work: general field service tools are built around service calls and construction platforms such as Procore around projects. BuildOps is built for both service and project work at commercial contractors, and Knowify adds progress billing and change orders for contractors on QuickBooks.
verticals.regulatory_notes:
Rules that affect what electrical software should record:

Licensing: states license electrical contractors and electricians differently, so track each license, its holder and its renewal date, especially if you work in more than one state.

National Electrical Code: states and cities adopt NEC editions on their own schedules and may add their own amendments, so note which edition applies where you work.

Workplace electrical safety: NFPA 70E sets workplace electrical safety practices, including arc flash, so keep training records for the techs who work on energized equipment.

Solar certification: NABCEP offers voluntary certifications for solar installers; check whether your state, utility or customers ask for one.

Permits: panel work, new circuits, service upgrades, EV chargers and generator installs can need permits, depending on your jurisdiction.

Federal tax credits (residential solar, home EV chargers): per the IRS, the Residential Clean Energy Credit (Section 25D) is not available for property placed in service after December 31, 2025, and the home EV charger credit (Section 30C) covered property placed in service through June 30, 2026, so new installs no longer qualify for either credit.

vertical_faqs.q: Which electrical software fits a 3-electrician shop?
vertical_faqs.a: For residential service work, Jobber (Connect plan from $99 a month billed annually) and Housecall Pro (Essentials, $149 a month billed annually with 5 users included) both publish prices and offer 14-day free trials. If most of your work is project work (commercial buildouts, multifamily), compare Knowify (Core from $99 a month billed annually; subcontracts and job costing start on Advanced) or BuildOps (quote-only), which handle progress billing for project work. Some shops with both kinds of work run a service tool for service calls and a project tool for buildouts.

vertical_faqs.q: How do electricians handle EV charger and solar quoting in software?
vertical_faqs.a: Service tools such as Jobber, Housecall Pro and ServiceTitan let you put a panel upgrade, circuit run and charger install on one quote as line items. Solar projects with batteries are designed and quoted in solar design tools: Aurora Solar, for example, sizes batteries and in September 2026 added quoting for EV chargers and batteries for US installers.

vertical_faqs.q: Does electrical software handle permits well?
vertical_faqs.a: Check before you buy. Ask each vendor to show permit tracking (application, status, inspection dates) and any connection to your municipality's permit portal in a demo. If a tool does not track permits, plan to keep a separate tracker.

vertical_faqs.q: Should commercial electrical contractors use service FSM or project software?
vertical_faqs.a: It depends on your work mix. Project work (commercial buildouts, multifamily construction, industrial) needs job costing, change orders and progress billing: BuildOps is built for commercial MEP contractors, Procore for commercial construction, and Knowify for contractors on QuickBooks. Service work (break/fix, panel upgrades, troubleshooting) runs on field service tools such as ServiceTitan or Housecall Pro. If you do a lot of both, compare a platform built for both, such as BuildOps, with running two tools.

vertical_faqs.q: How important is code-compliance documentation?
vertical_faqs.a: Photos of the work before it is covered, with the date and location, are a record if an inspector or customer asks later. Check how each tool files photos by job and whether it can export them. CompanyCam, a photo documentation app, lists integrations with ServiceTitan and Jobber, and Housecall Pro lists CompanyCam among its integrations.

verticals.name: Roofing
verticals.industry_context:
Roofing jobs run as projects, with measurements, a material order, a crew schedule and photos along the way. In areas hit by hail, wind or hurricanes, insurance work adds damage documentation, the carrier's estimate, supplements for work found during tear-off, and reconciling the final invoice against what the carrier approved.

AccuLynx and JobNimbus are built around the roofing workflow. AccuLynx keeps insurance jobs, supplements and documents in the job file but lists no Xactimate integration; JobNimbus connects to Xactimate and XactAnalysis only on its legacy financials. Roofr combines measurement reports with a CRM, proposals and payments for residential roofers.

Measurements and materials are where these tools save re-keying. AccuLynx orders EagleView, Hover, Geospan or GAF QuickMeasure reports that populate the estimate, JobNimbus connects to EagleView and Hover, and Roofr sells its own measurement reports. AccuLynx, JobNimbus and Roofr all list supplier ordering with ABC Supply, SRS Distribution and QXO (formerly Beacon).
verticals.buying_personas:
Which tools fit depends on your work mix and size.

Small retail roofers: Roofr has a free Starter plan and lists unlimited users on every plan, and general field service tools such as Jobber and Housecall Pro list roofing among their trades, though their feature lists in our data do not include insurance claim handling.

Insurance and storm restoration roofers: AccuLynx is built for established roofing companies (5 to 100 employees) running insurance claims and storm restoration, and JobNimbus for roofing, exterior and restoration contractors. Neither publishes prices. Compare how each handles supplements, carrier estimates and photo documentation, since AccuLynx lists no Xactimate integration and JobNimbus's works only on its legacy financials.

Larger operations: AccuLynx and JobNimbus both sell Enterprise plans; ask what each adds for multi-location reporting.

Commercial roofing (low-slope, single-ply) is closer to commercial construction. Procore is built for commercial construction projects, and BuildOps for commercial service and project work.
verticals.feature_priorities:
Features to test for roofing work:

Insurance job handling: damage photos, the carrier's estimate, supplements, claim status and the final invoice against the approved amount. AccuLynx keeps claim details, supplements and documents in the job file but lists no Xactimate integration; JobNimbus connects to Xactimate and XactAnalysis on its legacy financials.

Photo documentation: AccuLynx and JobNimbus include photo documentation and integrate with CompanyCam, which time- and location-stamps every photo and files it into a project.

Aerial measurements: AccuLynx orders EagleView, Hover, Geospan or GAF QuickMeasure reports with measurements flowing into the estimate, JobNimbus connects to EagleView and Hover, and Roofr sells its own measurement reports.

Material ordering: AccuLynx, JobNimbus and Roofr list supplier integrations with ABC Supply, SRS Distribution and QXO (formerly Beacon), so a signed job can become a material order without re-keying.

Door-to-door sales: AccuLynx has a door-to-door workflow and connects to SalesRabbit and Spotio.

Commissions: if your reps, project managers and crews are paid differently, check how each tool tracks commissions; AccuLynx lists commission tracking.
verticals.regulatory_notes:
Rules that affect what roofing software should record:

Licensing: states set their own rules for licensing roofers, and some do not license roofing at all, so check your state's contractor board and track each license where you work.

Fall protection: OSHA's fall protection rules for construction (29 CFR 1926 Subpart M) apply to roofing work, so keep training and equipment inspection records.

Workers' compensation: premiums depend on job classification and claims history, so keep safety training and incident records where you can find them.

Building codes: roof systems must meet local code requirements such as wind uplift and fire ratings, which vary by jurisdiction.

Insurance work: some states regulate contracts for insurance-paid roofing work, so check your state's rules and keep signed contracts with the job.

Permits: reroofs can need permits, depending on your jurisdiction; ask whether a tool tracks them.
verticals.seasonality:
Roofing demand follows the weather. Hail, wind and hurricane damage brings a run of insurance work to the areas hit, and in cold climates winter slows outdoor work.

After a storm, lead intake, inspections and claim paperwork can outrun the office, so check how a tool handles a surge of leads and photo uploads before the next one. Quieter months are the time to set up or switch software.

vertical_faqs.q: Which roofing software fits a residential storm restoration shop?
vertical_faqs.a: AccuLynx and JobNimbus are both built around residential roofing, including storm and insurance work. AccuLynx is built for roofing, with door-to-door workflows, commission tracking and AccuPay payments, and keeps supplements and insurance documents in the job file; it lists no Xactimate integration. JobNimbus also covers exterior and restoration work and connects to Xactimate on its legacy financials. Neither publishes prices, so get written quotes from both.

vertical_faqs.q: How important is Xactimate integration?
vertical_faqs.a: It matters if you work insurance claims, because Xactimate (Verisk) is estimating software used by insurance carriers and adjusters. Software that imports the carrier's estimate, compares it with yours and tracks supplements saves re-keying on every claim. Check the integration before you buy: JobNimbus connects to Xactimate and XactAnalysis only on its legacy financials, and AccuLynx lists no Xactimate integration.

vertical_faqs.q: Does roofing software handle commercial work well?
vertical_faqs.a: AccuLynx and JobNimbus are built around residential roofing, so a commercial roofer (low-slope, single-ply) should check the fit in a demo. Commercial roofing is closer to commercial construction project management: Procore is built for commercial construction projects, and BuildOps for commercial service and project work.

vertical_faqs.q: Should commercial roofing use BuildOps or AccuLynx?
vertical_faqs.a: They are built for different work. BuildOps is built for commercial contractors and covers service, project management and dispatch; AccuLynx is built for residential roofing companies running retail and insurance work. A company doing both could run AccuLynx for residential storm work and a commercial platform for commercial projects.

vertical_faqs.q: How do door-to-door storm-chasing operations handle software?
vertical_faqs.a: AccuLynx has a door-to-door workflow and connects to SalesRabbit and Spotio, so a rep can capture the lead and photos in the field and pass the job to production. JobNimbus runs a CRM with pipelines for the roofing sales cycle. Test the full flow in each demo: the rep signs the customer, the job is created, and production and the crew see it without re-entry.

verticals.name: General Contractors
verticals.industry_context:
General contractors run projects rather than service calls: a job lasts weeks or months, involves several trades, and carries schedules, change orders, permits and staged billing. That is why GC software is project management software rather than field service software.

The tools split by the kind of project. Buildertrend (which acquired CoConstruct in 2021 and moved its customers over) and JobTread are built for home builders, remodelers and specialty contractors, with client portals and selections. Knowify is built around QuickBooks for trade contractors that need job costing, change orders and AIA progress billing. Procore is built for commercial general contractors, specialty contractors and owners on complex multi-trade projects.

When a project bills in stages, the gap between paying subcontractors and suppliers and collecting each draw is a cash flow risk, so check how a tool links change orders, purchase orders and billing to the project budget.
verticals.buying_personas:
Which tools fit depends on the size and type of your projects.

Small remodelers and builders: Knowify (Core from $99 a month billed annually, 1 user) and JobTread ($199 a month base, 1 internal user included, with free customer and vendor portal users) publish their prices. Jobber lists general contracting among its trades and suits service-style jobs (quote, schedule, invoice, get paid).

Established residential builders and remodelers: Buildertrend and JobTread are built for home builders and remodelers, with client portals, selections and change orders. Buildertrend is custom-quoted with unlimited users; CoConstruct is no longer a separate product. Knowify, built on QuickBooks, suits contractors who keep their books there; job costing, the client portal and subcontracts start on its Advanced plan.

Commercial general contractors: Procore is built for commercial construction, with drawings, RFIs, submittals, budgeting and BIM integration, and is priced by annual construction volume with unlimited users.
verticals.feature_priorities:
Features to test for general contracting:

Subcontractor coordination: schedules for each trade, purchase orders, pay applications, lien waivers and document sharing. Buildertrend lists subcontractor management, Knowify includes subcontracts from its Advanced plan, and JobTread handles vendors and purchase orders.

Change orders: capture the change with the customer's signature and update the budget and remaining payments. Buildertrend, JobTread, Knowify and Procore all include change orders.

Progress billing (AIA G702/G703): Knowify lists AIA and progress billing; ask Buildertrend, JobTread and Procore to show their pay-application format in a demo.

Client portal: custom home and remodel clients can see schedules, selections, photos and budget updates in a portal instead of email. Buildertrend and JobTread both include client portals.

Material ordering: JobTread connects to The Home Depot, SRS Distribution and QXO, and Buildertrend to The Home Depot.
verticals.regulatory_notes:
Rules that affect what GC software should record:

Licensing: states set their own rules for licensing general contractors, including dollar thresholds in some, so track each license where you work.

Safety: OSHA's construction standards (29 CFR 1926) cover fall protection, scaffolding, excavation and electrical safety, so keep training and incident records by project.

Permits and inspections: track which permits each project needs, who pulled them and when inspections are due, so none lapse.

Lien laws vary by state: software that tracks lien deadlines and conditional and unconditional waivers from each subcontractor helps you meet them.

Federal tax incentives (energy efficiency, accessibility): per the IRS, the Energy Efficient Home Improvement Credit (Section 25C) covered improvements made through December 31, 2025, and the builder credit for energy-efficient new homes (Section 45L) is described for homes acquired through June 30, 2026, so energy-efficiency work done now falls outside both. For accessibility work, the IRS still lists the Disabled Access Credit (Section 44) for eligible small businesses and a deduction of up to $15,000 a year for removing architectural barriers (Section 190), so job records that separate accessibility costs can help commercial clients with those claims.
verticals.seasonality:
Exterior and structural work depends on the weather, so in cold climates it slows in winter while interior remodels continue. Weather delays also move schedules, so check how a tool shifts a schedule and notifies subcontractors and clients when one task slips.

Your own project history shows when new work arrives and when crews are busiest; plan a software change for a quieter stretch.

vertical_faqs.q: Should a remodeling business use Jobber or Buildertrend?
vertical_faqs.a: It depends on the kind of job. Jobber is built for service-style work: quote, schedule, invoice and get paid. Buildertrend is built for residential projects that run for weeks or months, with schedules, selections, change orders with homeowner approval, subcontractor coordination and a client portal. If most of your jobs are multi-week projects with subcontractors and change orders, compare Buildertrend, JobTread and Knowify.

vertical_faqs.q: What's the difference between Buildertrend and Procore?
vertical_faqs.a: Buildertrend is built for residential builders, remodelers and specialty contractors, with a homeowner-facing client portal and selections. Procore is built for commercial general contractors, specialty contractors and owners on complex multi-trade projects, with drawings, RFIs, submittals, budgeting and BIM integration, and is priced by annual construction volume with unlimited users. Pick by your main type of work.

vertical_faqs.q: Does Knowify replace QuickBooks?
vertical_faqs.a: No. Knowify is built on QuickBooks, with a two-way sync to QuickBooks Online and to QuickBooks Desktop (Desktop sync is on the Enterprise plan). Knowify handles project management, change orders, time tracking and progress billing; QuickBooks keeps the books.

vertical_faqs.q: How do GCs handle sub-contractor coordination in software?
vertical_faqs.a: Buildertrend lists subcontractor management, Knowify includes subcontracts from its Advanced plan, JobTread covers vendor management and purchase orders, and Procore is built for complex multi-trade commercial projects. In a demo, check how each handles subcontractor documents (W-9, certificate of insurance, license), schedule notifications when their work is due, purchase orders and pay applications, and lien waiver tracking.

vertical_faqs.q: Is project management software worth the cost for a 2-person remodeling business?
vertical_faqs.a: It depends on how many projects you run at once and how often change orders and subcontractor mix-ups cost you money. Buildertrend is now custom-quoted (its last published entry tier was $199 a month); Knowify's Core plan ($99 a month billed annually, $149 month to month) and JobTread ($199 a month base) publish their prices. Jobber and Housecall Pro are built for service jobs, so check change orders, subcontractors and progress billing before you use one for multi-week projects.

verticals.name: Landscaping & Lawn Care
verticals.industry_context:
Landscaping and lawn care businesses do three kinds of work: recurring maintenance (mowing, fertilizing, seasonal cleanups), commercial grounds contracts, and design-build projects such as installations, hardscaping and irrigation. Recurring work runs on crews and routes, so route planning, crew time tracking and recurring billing matter more than job-by-job dispatch.

General field service tools such as Jobber and Housecall Pro list landscaping among their trades, and Jobber is built for small and mid-size crews rather than large multi-location operations. Landscaping platforms add crew and route features: geo-tagged or GPS-stamped crew time (Aspire, LMN), route optimization (RealGreen's Dynamic Routing, Service Autopilot from its Pro plan), crew photos and weather notes (LMN), chemical tracking (Service Autopilot from Pro), and equipment maintenance tracking (Aspire).

Where it snows, snow and ice work changes routing, dispatch and billing for the winter. Aspire, LMN and Service Autopilot all cover snow work.
verticals.buying_personas:
Which tools fit depends on your crew count and the mix of residential, commercial and snow work.

Solo operators and small crews: Yardbook has a free Starter plan (with a 1% fee on online customer payments), Jobber's Core plan starts at $29 a month billed annually, and Service Autopilot's Startup plan is $49 a month on annual rates plus a sign-up fee.

Multi-crew maintenance companies: Aspire (a ServiceTitan company, built for established multi-crew companies), LMN, RealGreen and Service Autopilot are built around crews, routes and recurring work. Compare crew time tracking, route optimization and recurring billing in a demo.

Large commercial operations: Aspire covers grounds maintenance, landscape construction and snow and ice management with no limit on users, LMN's Enterprise plan targets multi-location companies, and RealGreen's Enterprise package includes unlimited licenses.

Tree care companies: SingleOps is sold by Granum as its tree care product, with a tree inventory on a map of each property.
verticals.feature_priorities:
Features to test for landscaping work:

Crew time tracking: start and stop times at each property feed job costing. Aspire's crew app records geo-tagged time, and LMN Crew records hours with GPS timestamps.

Route optimization for recurring routes: RealGreen's Dynamic Routing and Service Autopilot (from its Pro plan) include route optimization; test it on one of your real route days.

Recurring billing: weekly mowing, monthly maintenance and seasonal contracts need automatic billing, retries for failed payments, and a portal where customers can see and pay invoices. LMN, RealGreen and Yardbook (a branded portal on its Enterprise plan) list customer portals.

Photos: before and after photos filed by property help with commercial and HOA clients who are not on site. LMN's crew app attaches photos to each job.

Weather changes: rain and storms move work. Aspire texts clients about weather-driven schedule changes on snow work, and LMN Crew lets crews log weather notes.

Snow work: event-triggered dispatch and billing by push, event, inch or season. Service Autopilot bills flat rate, per push, per event, per inch or hourly.
verticals.regulatory_notes:
Rules that affect what landscaping software should record:

Pesticide applicator licensing: states license applicators for fertilizer, weed control and pest applications, so track each license, its expiry date and any continuing education it requires.

Pesticide product registration: states register the pesticide products that can be used there, so check that the products in your setup are registered in each state you work in.

Commercial driver licensing: whether a crew driver needs a CDL depends on the weight of the truck and trailer.

Employment records: US employers must complete Form I-9 for every hire, and businesses using H-2B seasonal workers have their own documentation requirements.

Safety: keep training records for equipment, chainsaw and chemical handling work.

Noise: check local rules before scheduling early-morning starts.
verticals.seasonality:
Landscaping follows the growing season: spring cleanups and the first treatments, steady mowing and maintenance through summer, leaf cleanup in fall, and, where it snows, snow and ice work in winter. How long each season runs depends on your climate.

Software needs change with the season, from recurring routes in summer to event-triggered dispatch in a snowstorm. The off-season is the time for contract renewals, route planning and setting up or switching software.

vertical_faqs.q: Which landscaping software fits a 3-crew operation?
vertical_faqs.a: Service Autopilot, LMN and Jobber are places to start. LMN is built for landscaping, with crew time tracking and crew routing (Starter is $297 a month for companies under 10 employees, plus an onboarding fee), and Service Autopilot is built for route-based services, with route optimization from its Pro plan ($199 a month on annual rates). Jobber (Connect plan from $99 a month billed annually) is a general home service tool that lists landscaping among its trades. Compare crew time tracking, routing and recurring billing on one of your real weeks.

vertical_faqs.q: Does Aspire work for residential landscaping or just commercial?
vertical_faqs.a: Aspire is built for established landscaping companies with multiple crews: grounds maintenance, landscape construction, and snow and ice management. It is priced by quote with no limit on users, and ServiceTitan agreed in 2021 to acquire it. Smaller residential operations that want published prices can compare LMN, Service Autopilot or Yardbook.

vertical_faqs.q: How do landscaping operations handle snow plowing software?
vertical_faqs.a: Aspire, LMN and Service Autopilot all cover snow and ice work, and Service Autopilot can bill flat rate, per push, per event, per inch or hourly. Snow dispatch is triggered by the storm rather than scheduled, billing differs (per push, per inch or seasonal contracts), and routes cover several properties per event, so test a storm day in the demo.

vertical_faqs.q: What about crew time tracking with non-English speakers?
vertical_faqs.a: If your crews work in Spanish, check the crew app's languages before you buy: LMN's crew app runs in English and Spanish. For any other language, ask each vendor, and have a crew lead try the app during the trial.

vertical_faqs.q: How important is photo documentation in landscaping?
vertical_faqs.a: It matters for commercial and HOA accounts where the customer is not on site: before and after photos filed by property show the work was done and help settle disputes. LMN's crew app attaches photos to each job; check how any general field service tool you consider files crew photos by property.

verticals.name: Cleaning Services
verticals.industry_context:
Cleaning businesses fall into three groups with different software needs: residential house cleaning on recurring schedules, commercial janitorial contracts, and specialty work such as move-out, post-construction, carpet or window cleaning.

Residential cleaning runs on recurring appointments, so the core needs are recurring scheduling, automated reminders, online booking and automatic billing. ZenMaid and Automaid (formerly Launch27) are built for residential cleaning, and general tools such as Jobber and Housecall Pro list cleaning among their trades.

Otuvy (formerly CleanTelligent) is built for commercial cleaning contractors that need site inspections, work orders and reports to share with clients, and Aspire has served commercial cleaning companies since 2021.

Water and fire damage cleanup is insurance-paid restoration work, which has its own software on our restoration page.
verticals.buying_personas:
Which tools fit depends on whether you clean homes or commercial buildings, and how big you are.

Solo cleaners and small residential teams: ZenMaid starts at $19 a month (up to 40 appointments a month), Jobber's Core plan at $29 a month billed annually, and Automaid at $75 a month with unlimited users.

Growing residential companies: compare ZenMaid Pro or Pro Max (unlimited appointments, GPS tracking and payroll from Pro), Automaid (cleaner mobile apps on the $299 Plus plan) and Jobber Connect or Grow. Recurring billing and crew scheduling are the features to test.

Commercial janitorial: Otuvy is built for site inspections, work orders and client reporting, and Aspire covers commercial cleaning with no limit on users.

Franchise and multi-location brands: Vonigo is built for franchise systems and multi-location home service companies, with central pricing and a workspace for each location.

Team management: Connecteam is a workforce app (time clock, scheduling, chat) that runs alongside a field service tool rather than replacing it.
verticals.feature_priorities:
Features to test for cleaning work:

Recurring scheduling and billing: weekly or every-other-week cleanings, reminders and automatic billing. ZenMaid and Automaid are built around recurring scheduling and automated reminders, and Jobber supports recurring jobs and visits.

Customer self-service: a portal where customers can manage bookings and update payment details takes calls off the office. Automaid includes a customer login where clients manage bookings, update cards and rebook, and Jobber includes a client portal; we did not find a customer self-service portal on ZenMaid's product pages.

Online booking: Jobber, Housecall Pro, ZenMaid (booking forms from Pro) and Automaid all offer online booking; Automaid's booking form shows a price as customers enter their home details.

Crew tracking: ZenMaid has GPS tracking and payroll from its Pro plan, and Automaid lists a payroll calculator and route optimization from its scheduler.

Photos and checklists: ZenMaid's cleaner app records notes and photos and its Pro plan adds digital checklists; Otuvy runs inspections from templates for commercial clients.

Financing: Jobber's Wisetack financing excludes residential and commercial cleaning businesses, so check another option if you sell large jobs on payment plans.
verticals.regulatory_notes:
Rules that affect what cleaning software should record:

Chemical safety: OSHA's Hazard Communication Standard covers employers whose workers use hazardous chemicals, with an exemption for consumer products used the way a consumer would use them. Where it applies, keep safety data sheets and training records.

Employment records: US employers must complete Form I-9 for every hire.

Bonding and insurance: if customers ask for proof of bonding or insurance, keep certificates where office staff can send them quickly.

Business licensing: requirements vary by city and state, so track each license and its renewal date if you work in more than one jurisdiction.

vertical_faqs.q: Which software fits a 5-crew residential cleaning operation?
vertical_faqs.a: ZenMaid, Automaid (formerly Launch27) and Jobber are places to start. ZenMaid (from $19 a month; unlimited appointments from Pro at $39 a month) and Automaid (from $75 a month with unlimited users; cleaner mobile apps on the $299 Plus plan) are built for residential cleaning, with recurring scheduling, automated reminders and online booking. Jobber (Connect plan from $99 a month billed annually) is a general home service tool that lists cleaning among its trades. All three offer 14-day free trials, so run a real week of recurring cleanings through each.

vertical_faqs.q: Does cleaning software handle commercial janitorial well?
vertical_faqs.a: Residential cleaning tools are built around recurring home appointments; commercial janitorial adds night work, multiple sites, monthly contracts and quality reporting for building clients. ZenMaid's own entry says it is built for maid services rather than commercial janitorial work. For commercial work, compare Otuvy (formerly CleanTelligent), built for site inspections, work orders and client reports, and Aspire, which has served commercial cleaning companies since 2021.

vertical_faqs.q: How important is customer self-service for cleaning operations?
vertical_faqs.a: A portal where customers skip a week, add a deep clean or update payment details takes those calls and texts off the office. Automaid (formerly Launch27) and Jobber include customer portals; we did not find one on ZenMaid's product pages. Confirm what each tool lets customers change themselves before you buy.

vertical_faqs.q: Should specialty cleaning (restoration, post-construction) use cleaning software or restoration software?
vertical_faqs.a: Water and fire damage work is insurance-paid restoration, with moisture readings, drying logs and carrier documentation, so it runs on restoration software (see our restoration page). Post-construction and move-out cleans are one-time jobs that cleaning and general field service tools can schedule and invoice.

vertical_faqs.q: How do cleaning operations handle no-shows and cancellations?
vertical_faqs.a: Automated reminders before each visit and an easy way to reschedule cut the back-and-forth. ZenMaid and Automaid (formerly Launch27) send automated text and email reminders, and Jobber sends automated follow-ups. Check how each tool handles a skipped visit in a recurring series before you buy.

verticals.name: Pest Control
verticals.industry_context:
Pest control software runs routes, recurring service, chemical records and billing for pest control companies. If you sell recurring service plans (monthly, every other month or quarterly), the software has to run routes and recurring billing, not just one-off jobs.

Pest platforms are built around that model. FieldRoutes, PestPac and GorillaDesk list routing or route optimization and chemical tracking, and ServSuite is now sold by FieldRoutes. General field service tools such as Jobber and Housecall Pro list pest control among their trades, but their feature lists in our data do not include chemical logs.

If your plans come in tiers (for example a basic plan and a premium plan with extra services such as mosquito or rodent work), check how each platform models plan tiers, visit frequency and upgrades in a demo.

Chemical records: each state sets what pesticide applicators must record and how long records are kept, so check your state's rules. FieldRoutes lists chemical and product tracking, PestPac chemical tracking and inventory, and GorillaDesk chemical data and material use reports.

Door-to-door sales: FieldRoutes traces back to TextRoutes, a door-to-door sales app, and its packages include mobile sales tools.
verticals.buying_personas:
Which tools fit depends on your size and whether you want published prices.

Solo operators and small companies: GorillaDesk publishes month-to-month pricing per route (from $49 a month), includes chemical logs and offers a 14-day free trial. The larger pest platforms quote on request.

Multi-route companies: PestPac (from WorkWave), FieldRoutes (formerly PestRoutes, a ServiceTitan company) and ServSuite (now sold by FieldRoutes, which steers new buyers to its own platform) are the quote-based pest platforms to compare. Compare route optimization, chemical records and recurring billing in a demo.

Large and multi-branch operators: PestPac's Enterprise package adds multi-branch management and API integrations, FieldRoutes names large pest brands such as Aptive and Fox Pest Control among its customers, and GorillaDesk's Growth plan adds multi-branch support.
verticals.feature_priorities:
Features to test for pest control work:

Route optimization: ordering each day's stops to cut drive time. FieldRoutes lists route optimization in both packages, PestPac from its Professional package, and GorillaDesk adds drive-time routing on Pro.

Chemical records: what was applied, where, how much, by whom and for which pest. Record-keeping rules vary by state, so check your state's rules. FieldRoutes, PestPac and GorillaDesk all include chemical tracking; without it you keep these records by hand.

Recurring billing: monthly or quarterly billing, retries for failed payments, plan changes and a customer portal. FieldRoutes has billing with AutoPay and a customer payment portal, and PestPac's customer portal is CustomerConnect.

Customer messages: visit reminders, reschedules and service-completion notices. FieldRoutes sends automated reminders, and GorillaDesk sends automated emails and texts.

Termite work: PestPac submits Sentricon reports and fills in WDI/WDO and NPMA-33 forms in the field, and FieldRoutes lists Sentricon integration.
verticals.regulatory_notes:
Rules that affect what pest control software should record:

Applicator licensing: states certify and license pesticide applicators, and restricted-use pesticides can only be applied by or under a certified applicator, so track each tech's license, its expiry date and continuing education.

Application records: each state sets what applicators must record (such as the product and its EPA registration number, the amount, the location, the applicator and the date) and how long records are kept.

Product registration: pesticide products must be registered for use in each state, so check the products in your setup against each state you work in.

Termite inspections: wood-destroying insect (WDI/WDO) inspections are reported on set forms such as NPMA-33, so check that your software fills in the forms your state and customers use; PestPac fills in WDI/WDO and NPMA-33 forms, including California WDO forms.
verticals.seasonality:
Insect activity follows the weather, so the busy months for general pest service, and when termite swarms appear, depend on your climate.

Your own service history shows which months bring the most new customers and callbacks. Plan route changes, contract renewals and any software change for a quieter stretch.

vertical_faqs.q: Can general FSM tools (Jobber, Housecall Pro) work for pest control?
vertical_faqs.a: Jobber and Housecall Pro list pest control among their trades, but their feature lists in our data do not include chemical logs. Pest platforms (GorillaDesk, PestPac, FieldRoutes) are built around routes and chemical tracking. If you run recurring routes or need application records, test those workflows before choosing a general tool.

vertical_faqs.q: What's the difference between PestPac and FieldRoutes?
vertical_faqs.a: They are quote-based pest platforms from competing companies: PestPac is made by WorkWave, while FieldRoutes is a ServiceTitan company (ServiceTitan announced the acquisition in January 2022). PestPac covers termite and commercial work (Sentricon reporting, WDI/WDO forms, IPM and multi-unit support) and sells three packages, with route optimization from Professional and multi-branch management on Enterprise. FieldRoutes (formerly PestRoutes, which traces back to TextRoutes, a door-to-door sales app built in 2009) includes mobile sales tools and prices by your number of active customers. Both handle routing, billing and chemical tracking; pick based on your work mix, integration needs and the quotes you get.

vertical_faqs.q: How does chemical logging compliance actually work in software?
vertical_faqs.a: Pest platforms record the products applied on each visit: FieldRoutes lists chemical and product tracking, PestPac chemical tracking and inventory, and GorillaDesk chemical data, templates and material use reports. Your state's rules set what each record must hold (such as the product and its EPA registration number, target pest, location, amount, applicator and date), so confirm in a demo that the platform captures every field your state requires and can produce the report an inspector will ask for.

vertical_faqs.q: What about door-to-door sales workflows?
vertical_faqs.a: FieldRoutes traces back to TextRoutes, a door-to-door sales app built in 2009, and its packages include mobile sales and lead management tools. GorillaDesk lists a SalesRabbit integration, and PestPac adds lead management from its Professional package. If door-to-door sales matter to you, test the full flow in each demo: the rep signs the contract on a phone, the customer record is created, recurring billing starts and the first service is scheduled.

vertical_faqs.q: How important is route optimization for pest control?
vertical_faqs.a: Route optimization orders a day's stops to cut drive time, so a tech can fit more stops into a day. Pest platforms include it (FieldRoutes in both packages, PestPac from Professional, GorillaDesk's drive-time routing from Pro). Test it on one of your real route days before you rely on it.

verticals.name: Pool Service
verticals.industry_context:
Pool service runs on recurring visits, such as weekly or every other week, along a route. Each visit involves water testing and chemical dosing, so the software has to run routes, record chemical readings and bill recurring plans. Repairs and equipment work (pumps, filters, salt cells, heaters) come on top of the route.

Pool-specific tools are built for this. Skimmer records chemical readings and dosages, photos and service history on each visit, with route optimization on its Scaling Up plan. Pool Brain targets medium and large pool companies with alerts and technician scorecards, Pool Founder prices by technician count with unlimited pools, and Paythepoolman charges a base fee plus a fee per technician.

General field service tools such as Jobber and Housecall Pro list pool service among their trades, but Jobber's Wisetack financing excludes pool and spa businesses.

In climates where pools close for winter, the software has to pause billing for closed pools and restart service in spring.
verticals.buying_personas:
Which tools fit depends on how many pools and technicians you run.

Solo operators and small crews: pool tools publish low entry prices. Skimmer's Getting Started plan is $1 per serviced pool a month with a $49 minimum, Pool Founder's Solo plan is $49 a month for one tech, and Paythepoolman is $65 a month for one tech.

Growing companies: compare Skimmer (priced per serviced pool, with unlimited users) and Pool Brain (priced per technician, built for medium and large pool companies). The pricing models differ, so work out each at your pool count and tech count.

Large and multi-location groups: Skimmer for Enterprise is custom-priced for businesses servicing more than 1,000 pools a month, and Pool Brain targets multi-branch and franchise operators.
verticals.feature_priorities:
Features to test for pool service:

Route optimization: Skimmer's route optimizer comes with its Scaling Up plan, and Pool Brain, Pool Founder and Paythepoolman include route optimization.

Chemical records: each visit's readings, doses and the condition of the pool. Skimmer records readings and dosages on each visit, and its Scaling Up plan adds the Orenda LSI and dosing calculator; Pool Founder and Paythepoolman also log readings and calculate doses.

Photos: Skimmer's technician app records photos with each visit, and Paythepoolman attaches before-and-after video to service logs.

Recurring billing: automatic monthly billing, autopay and retries for declined cards. Pool Brain retries declined cards automatically, and Skimmer offers AutoPay.

Equipment and repairs: Skimmer includes work orders and office alerts, and Pool Brain lists equipment tracking and custom alerts, so a problem found on a visit can become a scheduled repair.
verticals.regulatory_notes:
Rules that affect what pool service software should record:

Chemical safety: pool chemicals such as chlorine fall under OSHA's Hazard Communication Standard for employers, so keep safety data sheets and training records for your techs.

Pesticide rules: pool sanitizers and algaecides are registered as pesticides with the EPA, so check whether your state requires a pesticide applicator license for commercial pool treatment.

Draining and refilling: check local rules before draining a pool.
verticals.seasonality:
Where pools close for winter, the year runs from spring openings through summer route service to fall closings, with billing paused or reduced for closed pools. In warm climates, route service runs all year.

Ask each vendor how it pauses billing for closed pools and restarts service in spring, and switch software in your quietest month.

vertical_faqs.q: Should pool service operators use Skimmer or general FSM software?
vertical_faqs.a: Pool-specific software such as Skimmer logs chemical readings and dosages, photos and service history on each visit, and its Scaling Up plan adds route optimization. General tools such as Jobber and Housecall Pro list pool service among their trades, though Jobber's Wisetack financing excludes pool and spa businesses. Compare the chemical logging and route tools on a real route day.

vertical_faqs.q: How important is chemical tracking for pool service?
vertical_faqs.a: A record of each visit's readings and doses shows what was done if a customer questions the water or the bill. Pool platforms (Skimmer, Pool Brain, Pool Founder, Paythepoolman) build chemical logging into each visit; with a general field service tool you would log it in notes or a form.

vertical_faqs.q: Can pool service software integrate with QuickBooks?
vertical_faqs.a: Yes. Skimmer syncs one way from Skimmer into QuickBooks Online (it does not list QuickBooks Desktop), Pool Brain has a two-way QuickBooks Online sync, and Pool Founder and Paythepoolman list QuickBooks syncs. Check which edition you use and what each one syncs.

vertical_faqs.q: How do pool service operations handle equipment service vs routine maintenance?
vertical_faqs.a: Equipment problems found on a route visit can be scheduled as repairs, either on the same tech's route or as a separate visit. Skimmer includes work orders and office alerts, and Pool Brain lists equipment tracking and custom alerts; ask each vendor to show how an equipment issue found on a visit becomes a scheduled repair.

vertical_faqs.q: Is pool service software different in seasonal vs year-round markets?
vertical_faqs.a: Where pools close for winter, the software has to handle openings and closings: pausing billing for closed pools, scheduling winterization and restarting service in spring. Ask each vendor how it pauses billing and restarts service.

verticals.name: Locksmith
verticals.industry_context:
Locksmith work includes lockouts (home, car and business), rekeying, lock installs, key duplication, and commercial hardware and access control. Lockouts are urgent calls, so how fast a call is answered and a tech dispatched matters more than recurring scheduling.

Workiz, founded by former locksmiths, is built around inbound, same-day calls, with a phone system and call masking, Genius Phone call transcription, Genius Answering for missed calls (by plan or add-on), and lead integrations with Google Local Services Ads, Angi, Thumbtack and Yelp. General field service tools such as Jobber and Housecall Pro list locksmith work among their trades and publish their prices.

Automotive key work depends on the vehicle, so check whether a tool has fields for make, model and year or whether you will keep them in job notes.
verticals.buying_personas:
Which tools fit depends on your size and how much of your work is urgent calls.

Solo locksmiths and small crews: Workiz is built around inbound, same-day calls; it quotes prices on request and offers a 7-day free trial. Jobber and Housecall Pro publish their prices and offer 14-day free trials. If you get leads from Google Local Services Ads, all three list an integration.

Multi-tech operations covering a wide area: the test is how fast the nearest available tech gets each call. Compare call routing, missed-call handling and dispatch from a phone during each trial.

Commercial hardware and access control work: check how each tool handles commercial accounts with several sites, purchase orders and payment terms.
verticals.feature_priorities:
Features to test for locksmith work:

Call handling: a phone system with call routing, a plan for missed and after-hours calls, and dispatch to the nearest available tech. Workiz includes a phone system and call masking, Genius Phone transcribes and summarizes calls, and Genius Answering (by plan or add-on) answers missed calls and books jobs.

Lead sources: Workiz brings in leads and bookings from Google Local Services Ads and Reserve with Google, plus Angi, Thumbtack and Yelp; Jobber and Housecall Pro also list Google Local Services Ads integrations.

Clear quotes: itemized quotes that the customer approves before work starts help avoid price disputes on the doorstep.

Vehicle details: for automotive work, a place to record make, model and year on each job.

Mobile workflow: techs work from the van, so accepting jobs, updating status and taking payment should all work on a phone. Workiz's mobile app is built for accepting jobs, updating status and taking payment.
verticals.regulatory_notes:
Rules that affect what locksmith software should record:

Licensing: some states license locksmiths and require a background check, so check your state's rules and track each license and its renewal date.

Commercial door hardware: panic hardware and exit requirements for commercial doors come from fire and building codes, so note the requirements that apply when you quote commercial work.

Proof of ownership: if you check ID or proof of ownership before opening a home or vehicle, record it with the job.

vertical_faqs.q: Why do locksmiths look at Workiz?
vertical_faqs.a: Workiz is built around inbound, same-day calls rather than recurring scheduled work, and its founders worked as locksmiths. Genius Phone transcribes and summarizes calls, Genius Answering answers missed calls and books jobs (by plan or add-on), leads flow in from Google Local Services Ads, Angi, Thumbtack and Yelp, and the mobile app handles accepting jobs and taking payment. Workiz publishes no prices, so get a quote, and use its 7-day free trial on real calls.

vertical_faqs.q: How important is Google Local Services Ads for locksmiths?
vertical_faqs.a: It matters if you get calls through Local Services Ads, which appear at the top of Google search results where they run. Jobber, Housecall Pro and Workiz list Google Local Services Ads integrations. Whatever you use, track which ads produce booked jobs so you can see what each lead costs.

vertical_faqs.q: What's the typical response time for locksmith service?
vertical_faqs.a: We have no data on response times. Customers who are locked out want a firm arrival window, so quote one you can meet. Software helps on the part you control: answering the call, finding the nearest available tech and getting the job to that tech's phone, so test that flow during each trial.

vertical_faqs.q: Does Workiz publish its prices?
vertical_faqs.a: No. Workiz's Standard, Pro and Ultimate plans are quoted on request, and Genius Phone, Answering and Marketing are paid add-ons; it offers a 7-day free trial. Jobber and Housecall Pro publish their plans and offer 14-day free trials, so you can compare a published price with a Workiz quote.

verticals.name: Garage Door
verticals.industry_context:
Garage door work splits between service calls (springs, openers, cables, panels) and installations of new doors and openers, which are the larger jobs. Service calls are urgent for the customer, so call handling and dispatch matter; installations need clear quotes and a way to offer financing.

ServiceTitan and Workiz both list garage door work. Workiz is built around inbound, same-day calls; ServiceTitan is built for established businesses with larger teams that want depth in dispatch, marketing attribution and reporting. Neither publishes prices. Jobber and Housecall Pro list garage door work among their trades and publish their prices.

Parts on the truck decide whether a service call is finished on the first visit, so check inventory tracking: ServiceTitan lists inventory, Workiz offers inventory on some plans, and Jobber advertises no inventory management on any plan.
verticals.buying_personas:
Which tools fit depends on your size and your mix of service calls and installations.

Solo operators and small crews: Workiz is built around inbound, same-day calls (prices on request, 7-day free trial), and Jobber and Housecall Pro publish their prices and offer 14-day free trials.

Companies doing service and installations: compare Workiz's plans with Housecall Pro Essentials or MAX, and test both a same-day service call and an installation quote with financing during each trial.

Large and multi-location companies: ServiceTitan is built for established businesses with larger teams, and Vonigo for franchise systems and multi-location home service companies, with central pricing and a workspace for each location.
verticals.feature_priorities:
Features to test for garage door work:

Same-day dispatch: Workiz is built around the inbound call and same-day dispatch, and ServiceTitan's Dispatch Pro assigns jobs using technician skills, location, recent sales performance and conversion rates.

Financing for installations: ServiceTitan (GreenSky, Financeit, Service Finance), Housecall Pro and Jobber (Wisetack) and Workiz (Sunbit) all offer financing inside the job, so the customer can apply from the quote.

Truck inventory: springs and opener parts on each truck. ServiceTitan lists inventory, Workiz offers inventory on some plans, and Jobber advertises no inventory management.

Photos: before and after photos of each installation are a record of the work and of the opener's safety settings.
verticals.regulatory_notes:
Rules that affect what garage door software should record:

Opener safety: automatic residential garage door openers sold in the US must meet the entrapment-protection requirements of UL 325 under a federal rule (16 CFR Part 1211), so record the safety reverse and photo-eye checks on each install and service call.

Licensing: states set their own rules for licensing installation work, so check yours and track each license where you work.

Permits: door replacements can need permits, depending on your jurisdiction.

Spring safety: springs under tension can injure techs, so keep training records.

vertical_faqs.q: Which garage door software fits my business?
vertical_faqs.a: Workiz is built around inbound, same-day calls, which suits companies doing mostly service work. ServiceTitan is built for established businesses with larger teams that want depth in dispatch, marketing attribution and reporting. Neither publishes prices, so get quotes from both. Jobber and Housecall Pro list garage door work among their trades and publish their prices.

vertical_faqs.q: How important is consumer financing for garage door installations?
vertical_faqs.a: Installations are the larger jobs, and a monthly payment option in the quote lets the customer apply on the spot. ServiceTitan (GreenSky, Financeit, Service Finance), Housecall Pro and Jobber (Wisetack) and Workiz (Sunbit) all offer financing inside the job. Ask each lender who pays its fee.

vertical_faqs.q: How do garage door operations handle parts inventory?
vertical_faqs.a: Software with per-truck inventory shows which parts each truck carries before you dispatch. ServiceTitan lists inventory, Workiz offers inventory on some plans, and Jobber advertises no inventory management on any plan, so test truck stock during the trial if you rely on it.

vertical_faqs.q: Should garage door software handle service and installations differently?
vertical_faqs.a: If you do both, test both workflows: a same-day service call from phone to invoice, and an installation from quote (with financing) to install day. The first tests call handling and dispatch; the second tests quoting, financing and scheduling a crew.

vertical_faqs.q: What do multi-location garage door companies need from software?
vertical_faqs.a: Reporting across locations, consistent pricing and one customer record. ServiceTitan is built for established businesses with larger teams that want depth in reporting, and Vonigo for franchise systems and multi-location home service companies (garage door service among them), with central pricing and a workspace for each location. Both are quote-only.

verticals.name: Appliance Repair
verticals.industry_context:
Appliance repair is on-demand work: the customer calls when a refrigerator, washer or oven fails, a tech diagnoses it, and the job is either finished on the first visit or waits for a part.

When a job waits for a part, software that ties parts ordering to the schedule helps plan the return visit. ServiceTitan includes inventory and parts ordering from its mobile app, Workiz offers inventory on some plans, Service Fusion adds inventory from its Plus plan, and Jobber advertises no inventory management on any plan.

If you do authorized warranty work for manufacturers, those claims go through each manufacturer's own process, so ask whether a tool connects to the systems you use.
verticals.buying_personas:
Which tools fit depends on your size and how many parts you stock.

Solo operators and small crews: Workiz lists appliance repair among the businesses it serves and is built around inbound, same-day calls (prices on request, 7-day free trial). Jobber and Housecall Pro publish their prices and offer 14-day free trials, though Jobber advertises no inventory management.

Multi-tech companies: compare Workiz, Housecall Pro Essentials and Service Fusion (flat company price with unlimited users; inventory from Plus) on parts inventory and dispatch.

Larger companies: test parts inventory across vans and dispatch by skill (refrigeration, laundry, cooking) in a demo; ServiceTitan's Dispatch Pro assigns jobs using technician skills and location.
verticals.feature_priorities:
Features to test for appliance repair:

Parts inventory: per-van stock, parts ordered against a job, and the return visit scheduled when the part arrives. ServiceTitan includes inventory and parts ordering from its mobile app, and Workiz offers inventory on some plans.

Model and serial capture: a photo of the nameplate on the job record speeds up parts ordering.

Skills-based dispatch: techs differ by appliance type and brand. ServiceTitan's Dispatch Pro assigns jobs using technician skills and location.

Diagnostic fees: if you charge a diagnostic fee and credit it against the repair, check that the invoice handles it.

Warranty work: ask whether a tool connects to the manufacturer warranty systems you use.
verticals.regulatory_notes:
Rules that affect what appliance repair software should record:

EPA Section 608: technicians who open the refrigerant circuit of refrigerators, freezers and other appliances must be certified (Type I covers small appliances), so keep each tech's certification on file.

Licensing: some states license refrigeration or appliance work, so check your state's rules.

Recalls: manufacturers recall appliances from time to time, and records of model and serial numbers by customer let you contact the customers affected.

vertical_faqs.q: Does Workiz fit appliance repair?
vertical_faqs.a: Workiz is built around inbound, same-day calls, and it lists appliance repair among the businesses it serves. It offers inventory on some plans and publishes no prices, so get a quote. Jobber and Housecall Pro also list appliance repair among their trades, but Jobber advertises no inventory management, which matters if you stock parts.

vertical_faqs.q: How important is manufacturer warranty integration?
vertical_faqs.a: It matters if you do authorized warranty work. Each manufacturer has its own warranty claim process, so ask any field service vendor whether it connects to the warranty systems you use; otherwise plan to work in both.

vertical_faqs.q: How do appliance repair operations handle parts inventory?
vertical_faqs.a: Check whether a tool tracks stock per van, orders parts against a job and schedules the return visit when the part arrives. ServiceTitan includes inventory and parts ordering from its mobile app, Workiz offers inventory on some plans, Service Fusion adds inventory from its Plus plan, and Jobber advertises no inventory management.

verticals.name: Handyman Services
verticals.industry_context:
A handyman business takes on varied small jobs (repairs, drywall, carpentry, fixture installs, minor remodeling), so the software has to make quoting, scheduling and invoicing quick across many job types rather than go deep on one trade.

Some handyman work is billed by the hour and some at a set price, so check that a tool handles time-and-materials invoices as well as fixed quotes.

If you get leads from platforms such as Angi, Thumbtack or Yelp, check which tools connect to them: Workiz lists Angi, Thumbtack and Yelp integrations, Contractor+ lists Angi and Thumbtack, Housecall Pro lists Thumbtack, and Jobber can connect other tools through Zapier.
verticals.buying_personas:
Which tools fit depends on your size and budget.

Solo operators: Contractor+ has a free Freedom plan (up to 5 estimates or invoices a month), Joist's Basics plan is $8.34 a month billed annually or $10 billed monthly (up to 5 documents a month), Jobber's Core plan starts at $29 a month billed annually, and Housecall Pro's Basic plan is $59 a month billed annually.

Small teams: compare Jobber Connect or Grow and Housecall Pro Essentials (5 users included) for scheduling several techs and recurring property maintenance.

Larger teams: Jobber Plus, Housecall Pro MAX (8 users included, then a fee per user) and Service Fusion (a flat company price with unlimited users) are the higher plans to compare.
verticals.feature_priorities:
Features to test for handyman work:

Scheduling by skill: different techs handle different work, so check whether a tool lets you assign jobs by skill rather than just the next free slot.
